messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: realtime-serving SLO degradation detected in us-west-2 (p95/p99 elevated) :rotating_light:
incident-bot: key symptoms: streaming stalls, tail latency spikes, increased error budget burn. Auto-mitigation attempted: fallback routing to 'small-quant' but still impacted.
incident-bot: summary metrics:
```
p95: baseline 120ms -> 380ms
p99: baseline 900ms -> 2600ms
streaming stalls: 0.3% -> 6.8%
prefixcache hitrate: 92% -> 11%
```
incident-bot: suspect: recent prefix-hash rollout (prefix-scheme v3) deployed 00:58 UTC to ~80% of routing plane.

alice.oncall: ack - I'm on it. pulling traces and recent deploys now. @carla can you pull cache telemetry dashboard?

carla.sre: looking. confirmed hitrate collapse started ~01:02 UTC coincident with a canary shard flip. link: https://graf.redwood.internal/d/pc/prefix-cache?from=01:00&to=02:30
carla.sre: cache eviction + namespace churn visible. lots of 404s from prefetch path.

ben.runtime: i rolled the prefixhash PR (rollout-id: rollout-2026-03-15-7) at 00:58, can confirm traffic split 20/80 -> 80/100 by 01:05 due to gradual ramp. I didn't see the eviction numbers in staging.

alice.oncall: okay timeline makes sense. is there a safe quick rollback?

deploy-bot: rollback command available: `deploy rollback rollout-2026-03-15-7 --target=all`

ben.runtime: rollback is safest short-term. but we need to warm the cache afterwards or we'll have transient low-hitwave. two options:
- rollback now, let older prefix scheme serve (fastest)
- or pin live fallback to previous prefix variant while we warm (more surgical)

carla.sre: if we rollback, prefetch queue will spike because requests will repopulate caches. we should increase prefetch worker concurrency and set temporary TTL bump to reduce churn.

alice.oncall: do we have customer impact? dave/support take this

dave.support: monitoring for incoming tickets - a handful of realtime customers reported "stream stalls" and elevated response times, no major revenue-impacting SLA escalations yet but a few paying accounts on Dedicated reported p99 > 2s in our incident form. reaching out to top 10 customers now.

eva.prod: flagging product - this is affecting streaming UX (live transcription, chat). if rollback will cause brief 30-90s downtime for long-lived streams we need to notify.

ben.runtime: quick mitigation I'd run now:
1) `deploy rollback rollout-2026-03-15-7 --target=canary` (stop rollout)
2) disable prefix-scheme v3 routing in the router: `routerctl feature toggle prefix_v3 false`
3) increase prefetch workers: `prefetchctl scale --pool=stream-prefetch --replicas=4`
4) temporarily set prefix TTL to 15m instead of 5m: `kvctl set-prefix-ttl --prefix=live* --ttl=15m`

carla.sre: prepared a playbook block for the TTL change, but note: TTL bump will delay full recovery of stale keys; it's a tradeoff to avoid repeated misses. also enabling in-memory warmup: `warmupctl start --pattern=hotpaths --rate=200/s`

alice.oncall: execute steps 1 and 2 now? I can run router toggle. who will run rollback?

ben.runtime: i will run rollback and watch deploy-bot.

deploy-bot: deploying rollback to canary...

deploy-bot: rollback to previous prefix routing at 01:18:42 UTC - canary stopped, holding rollout.

ben.runtime: now toggling router feature to disable v3
carla.sre: applying TTL bump and scaling prefetch pool
carla.sre: warmup started (rate=200/s)

alice.oncall: metrics after rollback/toggles (01:21 UTC):
```
p95 -> 180ms (from 380ms)
p99 -> 1100ms (from 2600ms)
streaming stalls -> 2.1% (from 6.8%)
prefix hitrate -> 45% (from 11%)
```
alice.oncall: still above SLO but trending toward recovery.

dave.support: customer outreach: initial messages sent to affected accounts, responses from 3 customers acknowledging, none escalated to legal/SLA yet.

eva.prod: good. prepare a short status note for customers if p99 remains >1s after 30m.

ben.runtime: root cause hypothesis: prefix-v3 changed key salting/namespace mapping which caused massive keyspace shift; our prefetch/warmup assumptions didn't cover the new mapping so misses cascaded and caused heavy backend load and streaming stalls. need deeper postmortem.

carla.sre: agreed. follow-ups:
- audit rollout gating (canary ramp triggers)
- add synthetic probes for prefix hotpath after schema changes
- add automated warmup on prefix mapping change

alice.oncall: handing off to next on-call for bridge and post-incident cleanup. @frank.oncall you're up, please keep watch and coordinate with Ben/Carla for the follow-ups.

frank.oncall: ack taking over. will monitor for next 2h and keep the bridge open. please post any logs/traces you gather in this thread.

ben.runtime: collecting trace: `s3://redwood-traces/2026-03-15/prefix-rollout/trace-5054321111.json`

carla.sre: dump of evictions and prefetch backlog uploaded: `s3://redwood-ops/evictions/5054321111/`

alice.oncall: incident severity downgraded to Sev-2 at 01:35 UTC as surface area reduced but still tracking until p99 < 1s for 30m.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: SLO trending down. next check at 01:50 UTC.

frank.oncall: noted. will coordinate postmortem owner (ping @ben.runtime and @carla.sre) and schedule 1-hour blameless review tomorrow.

alice.oncall: thanks team. handing complete. :thumbsup:
